title: GovernanceCertification predicate (v1)
description: The five-pillar predicate carried by an in-toto Statement inside a DSSE envelope. Derived from what build_predicate() actually emits, not from prose: governance_cert.py previously pointed at a schema path that did not exist, and a schema written from intent is how that happens. test_governance_certification.py asserts the emitted predicate still validates against this file, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

verdict.description: hold-approved: held by PreToolUse and then approved by a human. permit: the gate allowed it with no human step required.

risk.description: A grounding SIGNAL plus a human-facing light. Grounding grounds the POLICY; the light organises risk for a person and is not an automated decision.

enforced.description: The load-bearing pillar. NOTE what backs it: blocked_unless_permitted is emitted as a constant true, so the field carries no information on its own. What makes it true is the CALL PATH: hook.py mints only when a PreToolUse marker exists, verifies that marker's Ed25519 signature against this installation's key, and consumes it once. The signature covers the tool_use_id, so a genuine marker cannot be replayed against another action; an unsigned or altered one mints nothing and is reported through audit_drop. See test_hold_marker_signature.py.

oversight_certificate.description: A full portable oversight-certificate, embedded only when the [oversight-cert] extra is installed. Absent means not installed — never that oversight was absent.
